key_insight: BISECT counters spectral starvation in continual LoRA learning by dividing a fixed low-rank budget between shared invariant features and task-specific novelty.
engineering_relevance: The approach may support sequential updates to engineering vision models without inference overhead, but the abstract does not evaluate solid mechanics or constitutive modeling.
method: Build an invariant carrier from dominant modes of the joint historical-and-current Gram matrix.
Extract an orthogonal novelty complement using generalized Rayleigh whitening and complement projection.
Merge trained updates into the frozen backbone, gating invariant atoms by current-to-joint Rayleigh ratios and preserving novelty atoms at unit gain.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that historical null tails capture only 5.5% of incoming-task variance and that BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines across eight incremental settings on five vision datasets.
watch_item: Whitening stability and training-time spectral decomposition costs require assessment; zero added inference cost does not imply zero training overhead.
paper_title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
